record.locator: Questions13 and15, PDF pp.34 and40; Section3
record.statement: Under suitable nondegenerate iid passage-time assumptions, prove a fluctuation exponent strictly below1/2, identify the planar exponent as1/3, and establish a positive exponent in a suitable dimension.
record.statement_caveat: These closely related exponent-range targets are grouped. Different definitions using variances or stronger concentration must be specified before claiming equivalence.
record.title: Subdiffusive and KPZ passage-time fluctuation exponents

record.independent_check: The logarithm calculation is exact in the limit; the example has additive variances. It is not asserted to be FPP.
record.method: Subdiffusive and KPZ passage-time fluctuation exponents structural argument
record.obstruction: Known sublinear-variance estimates leave a polynomial-exponent gap. An additional power saving, and a matching lower bound for identification, are required.
record.result: A variance upper bound of order n/log n does not establish an exponent below1/2. Indeed log(n/log n)/(2log n) tends to1/2. Sums of floor(n/log n) independent mean-zero variance-one variables realize that variance order in an elementary model.

primary_source.complete_scope_in_own_words: On nearest-neighbour Z^d with iid nonnegative edge times, choose suitable edge-law conditions and an exponent definition; establish chi<1/2 for d>=2, the value chi=1/3 in the plane, and chi>0 in a suitable dimension.
primary_source.hypothesis_caveat: The source deliberately leaves suitable conditions and the meaning of the scaling asymptotic open; it provides no universal complete hypothesis package.
